Solve Solid Mechanics Problem 1 using legacy FEniCS (dolfin) with small-strain linear elasticity in 2D plane stress.

Discretize the rectangular domain Ω = (0, 1.0) × (0, 0.20) m using a uniform structured mesh with 20 cells in x and 4 cells in y.

Use a vector-valued continuous Lagrange finite element space of degree 1 for the displacement field u = (u_x, u_y).

Assemble the variational form using the 2D plane-stress constitutive law σ = λ_ps tr(ε) I + 2 μ ε with ε = sym(∇u) restricted to the 2D plane.

Set the shear modulus μ = E / (2·(1 + ν)) = 200e9 / 2.6, giving μ ≈ 7.6923076923 × 10¹⁰ Pa.

Set the reduced plane-stress Lamé parameter λ_ps = E·ν / (1 − ν²) = 200e9 × 0.30 / 0.91, giving λ_ps ≈ 6.5934065934 × 10¹⁰ Pa.

Use Young's modulus E = 200 GPa and Poisson's ratio ν = 0.30.

Do not use the 3D isotropic λ = E·ν / ((1 + ν)·(1 − 2·ν)) anywhere in the assembly; the plane-stress reduced law is the correct choice.

Apply a Dirichlet boundary condition u = (0, 0) on the left edge at x = 0.

Apply a prescribed displacement u = (0.001, 0) m on the right edge at x = 1.

Leave the top edge at y = 0.20 and the bottom edge at y = 0 traction-free.

Solve the resulting sparse linear system with a direct solver.

Produce a colour map of the scalar field u_x over the domain and save the figure as q1_ux.png.

Save the full displacement field u to an XDMF file for post-processing.
